A different tradition

Tanjore art

Thanjavur (Tanjore) painting is a centuries-old South Indian art form, traditionally used to depict deities, built from raised relief, inlaid stones, and rich color. The relief comes from cone work: a paste of chalk powder and gum, built up by hand into a raised 3D design, then finished with gold foil pressed over the top. It's a much slower, more physical process than oil.

Because the relief and stonework are three-dimensional, a flat print loses most of what makes a piece like this worth having, so these are made to order rather than sold as prints.

About

Painting between problem sets

I've been painting for as long as I can remember. I started out with acrylics, moved to oil about three years ago, and haven't looked back. There's something about the slower pace and the way the colors blend into each other that I just love. I do Tanjore art on the side too, which is a completely different kind of patience (gold foil does not forgive a rushed hand).

I'm an engineering student as well, and I sometimes get asked which one is "the real thing." Honestly, both are. Art isn't a phase I'm easing out of, it's just always been part of how I think, and it always will be. My degree happens to be in something else.

Most of what's here is recent work, made between Mumbai and Manchester. I'm always open to commissions, print orders, or freelance illustration work, so just reach out.
